title: Republican senator urges Trump to back US open-weight AI models amid industry debate

content_html:
By Courtney Rozen

WASHINGTON, Aug 14 (Reuters) - Republican Senator Jim Banks is urging the Trump administration to develop incentives to encourage U.S. ‌tech companies to develop open-weight AI models, according to a letter ‌released on Friday, adding to a growing debate over the industry's future.

Open-weight models are AI ​systems with publicly accessible core elements, such as Meta's Muse Glimmer, Nvidia's Nemotron and startup Thinking Machines' Inkling. Users can download and fine-tune them for specific tasks, and they can be cheaper for cost-conscious customers.

Closed-weight AI tools are generally regarded ‌as more capable, and their ⁠creators retain control over their components. Key examples include OpenAI's ChatGPT, Anthropic's Claude and Google's Gemini.

Open-weight AI models from Chinese ⁠firms are becoming increasingly popular in the U.S., prompting security concerns in Washington that Chinese companies could gain an edge in a segment of the AI ​industry.

Banks, ​a member of the Senate Armed Services ​Committee that oversees national security ‌issues, asked U.S. President Donald Trump's administration to devise options to "limit dependence" on Chinese-made open-weight models, adding that the U.S. government must also make it harder for those firms to use American semiconductors to build their products.

"America cannot afford to see Chinese open models proliferate and burrow into the ‌global economy only to be weaponized, like ​rare earths, at a time and place of ​China's choosing," Banks wrote ​in a letter to Trump's economic adviser Christopher Phelan.

With his ‌letter, Banks joins a debate that ​has split the ​tech industry. Nvidia and Meta, joined by dozens of U.S. tech companies and venture capital firms, urged policymakers in July not to restrict ​open-weight AI, while Anthropic ‌CEO Dario Amodei has said open-weight models could present a ​security risk, adding it is harder to monitor their usage.

(Reporting by ​Courtney Rozen; Editing by Nia Williams)

content_html_zh:
考特尼·罗森

路透华盛顿 8 月 14 日 - 根据周五发布的一封信，共和党参议员吉姆·班克斯 (Jim Banks) 敦促特朗普政府制定激励措施，鼓励美国科技公司开发开放权重人工智能模型，这加剧了对该行业未来日益激烈的争论。

开放权重模型是具有可公开访问核心元素的人工智能系统，例如 Meta 的 Muse Glimmer、Nvidia 的 Nemotron 和初创公司 Thinking Machines 的 Inkling。 用户可以下载它们并针对特定任务进行微调，而且对于注重成本的客户来说，它们可以更便宜。

封闭式人工智能工具通常被认为能力更强，并且它们的创建者保留对其组件的控制权。 关键例子包括 OpenAI 的 ChatGPT、Anthropic 的 Claude 和 Google 的 Gemini。

中国公司的开放式人工智能模型在美国越来越受欢迎，这引发了华盛顿的安全担忧，即中国公司可能在人工智能行业的某个领域获得优势。

班克斯是负责监督国家安全问题的参议院军事委员会成员，他要求美国总统唐纳德·特朗普政府制定方案，“限制”对中国制造的开放式模型的依赖，并补充说，美国政府还必须让这些公司更难使用美国半导体来制造其产品。

班克斯在给特朗普经济顾问克里斯托弗·费兰的信中写道：“美国不能看到中国的开放模式激增并深入全球经济，却在中国选择的时间和地点被武器化，比如稀土。”

通过这封信，班克斯加入了一场导致科技行业分裂的辩论。 Nvidia 和 Meta 以及数十家美国科技公司和风险投资公司在 7 月份敦促政策制定者不要限制开放权重人工智能，而 Anthropic 首席执行官达里奥·阿莫迪 (Dario Amodei) 表示开放权重模型可能会带来安全风险，并补充说监控其使用情况更加困难。

（考特尼·罗森报道；尼亚·威廉姆斯编辑）
